
ENGINE VIEW  (grafts — mounts in the ENGINE's derived mount namespace, NOT the
  payload's. The payload cannot see any of these; no profile can ask for one.)
  (an engine outside every grant this sandbox makes adds a fifth graft at /snug/engine/toolchain — whether
  this host needs one is a preflight answer, and --dry-run runs no preflight.)
  graft-ro    /snug/engine/conf                             (snug)
            from /tmpdir/snug-UID-PID/conf
            owned: the sandbox's own grants do not expose this host path — it
            passed G4 only because snug declared it its own for this run
            (EngineOwnedHostPaths)
            abuse: READ every configuration file snug generated for it — and
            only read them: this is the half of the run directory that is
            read-only, so an engine that is talked into writing cannot rewrite
            the storage, registry or signature policy it was started under, nor
            turn the deliberately EMPTY auth file into a usable one
            note: this graft's destination is created on the sandbox's own root
            tmpfs and IS visible to the payload — empty, and unwritable once /
            is remounted read-only. The mount namespace is private; the tmpfs
            superblock is not (ENGINE-NETNS.md §5.1).
  graft-rw    /snug/engine/runroot                          (snug)
            from /tmpdir/snug-engines-UID-sha256_5f724cfb226eb5b98f5cd51ec1ccf05a9d433cb3a5377cf8006f94b157ffe3a9/rr
            owned: the sandbox's own grants do not expose this host path — it
            passed G4 only because snug declared it its own for this run
            (EngineOwnedHostPaths)
            abuse: write into the engine's runroot, which is keyed by the TARGET
            DIRECTORY rather than by pid (podman's libpod database refuses a
            runroot that disagrees with the one it recorded), so a LATER run of
            the same project inherits whatever an earlier one left there
            note: this graft's destination is created on the sandbox's own root
            tmpfs and IS visible to the payload — empty, and unwritable once /
            is remounted read-only. The mount namespace is private; the tmpfs
            superblock is not (ENGINE-NETNS.md §5.1).
  graft-rw    /snug/engine/sock                             (snug)
            from /tmpdir/snug-UID-PID/sock
            owned: the sandbox's own grants do not expose this host path — it
            passed G4 only because snug declared it its own for this run
            (EngineOwnedHostPaths)
            abuse: create or replace the socket the container proxy dials — the
            engine must be able to bind it, which is why this half of the run
            directory is writable and the other half is not
            note: this graft's destination is created on the sandbox's own root
            tmpfs and IS visible to the payload — empty, and unwritable once /
            is remounted read-only. The mount namespace is private; the tmpfs
            superblock is not (ENGINE-NETNS.md §5.1).
  graft-rw    /snug/engine/store                            (snug)
            from /xdg-data/snug/engines/sha256_5f724cfb226eb5b98f5cd51ec1ccf05a9d433cb3a5377cf8006f94b157ffe3a9/storage
            owned: the sandbox's own grants do not expose this host path — it
            passed G4 only because snug declared it its own for this run
            (EngineOwnedHostPaths)
            abuse: write image layers into a store that PERSISTS across runs and
            is shared with every other sandbox on the SAME TARGET DIRECTORY,
            whatever profiles it selected — so a run with a narrow selection
            inherits what a broader one pulled, and a layer a container poisons
            outlives the sandbox that pulled it, and is there for the next run
            of the same project
            note: this graft's destination is created on the sandbox's own root
            tmpfs and IS visible to the payload — empty, and unwritable once /
            is remounted read-only. The mount namespace is private; the tmpfs
            superblock is not (ENGINE-NETNS.md §5.1).

  engine-owned host paths  snug created these for this run; a graft's Host may
                           name one under G4 even though no sandbox grant
                           exposes it (OwnEngineHostPath, the only writer):
    /tmpdir/snug-UID-PID/conf
    /tmpdir/snug-UID-PID/sock
    /tmpdir/snug-engines-UID-sha256_5f724cfb226eb5b98f5cd51ec1ccf05a9d433cb3a5377cf8006f94b157ffe3a9/rr
    /xdg-data/snug/engines/sha256_5f724cfb226eb5b98f5cd51ec1ccf05a9d433cb3a5377cf8006f94b157ffe3a9/storage
